Six functions call `check_scalar` directly. I found them by searching every non-test file under `sklearn/` and reading the call sites.

| Caller | Call site | How it gets the name |
|---|---|---|
| `PinballLoss.__init__` | `sklearn/_loss/loss.py:611` | imported from `sklearn.utils`, which re-exports it |
| `HuberLoss.__init__` | `sklearn/_loss/loss.py:678` | imported from `sklearn.utils` |
| `SpectralBiclustering._check_parameters` | `sklearn/cluster/_bicluster.py:533`, `:540` | imported from `sklearn.utils` |
| `GraphicalLassoCV.fit` | `sklearn/covariance/_graph_lasso.py:981` | imported directly |
| `SelectFromModel._check_max_features` | `sklearn/feature_selection/_from_model.py:324` | imported from `utils.validation` |
| `_ridge_regression` (a module-level function) | `sklearn/linear_model/_ridge.py:693` | imported directly |

I left out two places on purpose:
- **Passed as a value, not called:** `LinearModelCV.fit` (`_coordinate_descent.py:1693`) and `_BaseRidgeCV.fit` (`_ridge.py:2357`, `:2364`). Both only pass `check_scalar` into `functools.partial(...)` and then call the resulting wrapper.
